```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

`R2_glmm()` computes an adjusted coefficient of determination (R²) for linear and
generalized linear mixed models with Piepho's (2023) method. It works for `lmer`,
`glmer` and `glmmTMB` fits and picks the residual (distribution-specific) variance for
the model's family and link automatically.

```{r}
library(predictmeans)
args(R2_glmm)
```

With `over_disp = TRUE`, an observation-level random effect (one level per observation)
is treated as overdispersion and counted as residual variance.

## Example 1: body length (linear mixed model)

```{r}
data(Body_length)
str(Body_length)
mod_BodyL <- lmer(BodyL ~ Treatment + Habitat + Sex + (1|Population/Container),
                  data = Body_length)
R2_glmm(mod_BodyL)
```

## Example 2: egg counts (Poisson GLMM with overdispersion)

Each female has her own level of `individual` within `Container` and `Population`, so the
innermost random effect is observation-level and models overdispersion.

```{r}
data(Poisson_ind)
mod_poisson <- glmer(Egg ~ Treatment + Habitat + (1|Population/Container/individual),
                     family = "poisson", data = Poisson_ind)
R2_glmm(mod_poisson, over_disp = TRUE)
```

## Example 3: clinical trial (binomial GLMM, three links)

The `Clinical` data (Beitler & Landis 1985) give the number of favourable responses out
of the patients in each treatment group at each of eight clinics.

### Clinic-level data

```{r}
data(Clinical)
Clinical$Unfavorable <- Clinical$Total - Clinical$Favorable
fit_grp <- function(link)
  glmer(cbind(Favorable, Unfavorable) ~ Treatment + (1|Clinic/Treatment),
        family = binomial(link = link), data = Clinical)
R2_glmm(fit_grp("logit"))
R2_glmm(fit_grp("probit"))
R2_glmm(fit_grp("cloglog"))
```

### Patient-level (binary) data

The same data with one row per patient give the same fixed effects, but the residual
variance is now that of a Bernoulli outcome.

```{r}
idx <- rep(seq_len(nrow(Clinical)), Clinical$Total)
Clinical_N <- Clinical[idx, c("Clinic", "Treatment")]
Clinical_N$favour <- unlist(lapply(seq_len(nrow(Clinical)), function(i)
  rep(c(1, 0), c(Clinical$Favorable[i], Clinical$Unfavorable[i]))))
str(Clinical_N)
fit_pat <- function(link)
  glmer(favour ~ Treatment + (1|Clinic/Treatment),
        family = binomial(link = link), data = Clinical_N)
R2_glmm(fit_pat("logit"))
R2_glmm(fit_pat("probit"))
R2_glmm(fit_pat("cloglog"))
```

## References

Piepho, H.-P. (2023). An adjusted coefficient of determination (R²) for generalized
linear mixed models in one go. *Biometrical Journal*, 65(7), e2200290.
doi:10.1002/bimj.202200290

Nakagawa, S. and Schielzeth, H. (2013). A general and simple method for obtaining R²
from generalized linear mixed-effects models. *Methods in Ecology and Evolution*, 4,
133–142.

Beitler, P. J. and Landis, J. R. (1985). A mixed-effects model for categorical data.
*Biometrics*, 41, 991–1000.
